item.title: Nvidia raises sales outlook, says business can thrive without Huang
item.description: Nvidia raised its next fiscal year's revenue growth forecast to 75% and announced a $150 billion stock buyback expansion as interim CEO Colette Kress sought to reassure investors.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: Nvidia Corp sought to deliver a clear message during its first earnings update since the departure of longtime leader Jensen Huang: He is not coming back, and the company will be fine without him. The chip giant boosted its sales forecast for next year and vowed to improve its access to critical supplies, while tamping down speculation that Huang might return. The company also added $150 billion to its stock buyback programme. Investors initially applauded the news, sending the stock up as much as 5.4 per cent at one point. It later dipped into the red on alternative trading platform Blue Ocean. “Our supply is growing, our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed,” interim Chief Executive Officer Colette Kress said during a conference call with analysts on Tuesday. “We’ve got this.” It was a high-stakes moment for Kress, who took the reins last week after Huang’s ouster — a chaotic exit reportedly spurred by multiple extramarital affairs and concerns that he was targeted by a Chinese espionage plot. Nvidia has been the largest beneficiary of the artificial intelligence (AI) build-out, and Huang served as the industry’s biggest cheerleader. Now the company looks to ensure that its momentum will not be undermined by the controversy swirling around it. Revenue will grow 75 per cent in the next fiscal year, Nvidia said, up from a previous forecast of 70 per cent. Sales will be $130 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter, plus or minus 3 per cent. Analysts had estimated $125.3 billion on average. “It’s business as usual,” said Kress, who has been Nvidia’s chief financial officer for more than a decade. “We’ve engaged with our customers. We’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100 per cent behind us.” Nvidia has embarked on a search for a new permanent CEO. During the call, Chairman Harvey Jones dismissed the idea that Huang might return. “The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” he said, adding that executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles had been enlisted to find a new leader. Nvidia also said it would no longer ship its licensed Hopper data centre products to China, although the company had been allowed to offer those older-generation components under US export rules. At the firm's data centre division — its biggest source of revenue — sales more than doubled to $107.6 billion in the third quarter, which ended October 25. Total sales rose 103 per cent to $115.8 billion in the same period. Meanwhile, China's military is seeking advanced Nvidia chips for AI-enabled weapons as Chinese-made processors continue to lag US rivals, a congressional commission said in its annual report released on Wednesday.

Home / Finance / News / RBI may hike interest rates by 75 basis points by Q2 CY27: Goldman Sachs

RBI may hike interest rates by 75 basis points by Q2 CY27: Goldman Sachs Goldman Sachs expects RBI to raise rates by 75 bps by Q2 CY27 as inflationary pressures persist, slowing India's growth to 7.2%

Reserve Bank of India (Photo: Reuters)

PTI 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 18 2026 | 6:08 PM IST

Listen to This Article

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) may raise the benchmark interest rate by 75 basis points by the second quarter of calendar year 2027, as rising food prices and broadening inflationary pressures are likely to prompt monetary tightening, according to a Goldman Sachs Research report.   The interest rate hike is expected to moderate India's real GDP growth to 7.2 per cent in CY27, down from an estimated 7.9 per cent in CY26.   Goldman Sachs expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points in December, followed by another 50 basis points in the first half of CY27, taking the rate to 6.25 per cent by Q2 CY27, the report said.

"With headline inflation likely to remain slightly above 6 per cent through Q4 CY26 and Q1 CY27 in our forecasts, and price pressures broadening across core goods and services, we expect the RBI to continue its 'calibrated tightening' cycle,"Â the report said.   The RBI raised its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 per cent in the October policy, its first hike in nearly four years.   Also Read

RBI may need tighter monetary policy to contain persistent inflation premium

RBI likely to hike rates further by 50-75 basis points: Economists premium

Higher money growth does not translate into higher inflation in India premium

Goldman Sachs expects India's headline retail inflation to average 5.7 per cent in CY27, while core inflation is projected at 4.7 per cent, driven by higher food prices, weather disruptions associated with El Nino and elevated input costs.

Goldman Sachs Chief India Economist Santanu Sengupta said inflation has already breached the upper end of the RBI's target band, reaching 6.1 per cent in October.   He expects inflation to remain around 6 per cent over the next two quarters before gradually easing towards the early 5 per cent range by the end of the year.   Despite the anticipated monetary tightening, Goldman Sachs expects India's real GDP growth to remain robust at 7.2 per cent in CY27, moderating from an estimated 7.9 per cent in CY26.   The report said strong domestic demand, resilient private consumption and an emerging investment cycle in energy, materials and strategic manufacturing sectors would continue to support economic activity.

However, tighter financial conditions, higher corporate borrowing costs and fading effects of tax cuts could weigh on consumption and investment growth.   Goldman Sachs projected real investment growth at around 8.5 per cent in CY27, supported by sectors aligned with India's energy security, defence and supply-chain priorities.   On the external front, the current account deficit is expected to remain contained at around 1 per cent of GDP in CY26 and CY27, supported by robust services exports and remittances.   The report also forecast the rupee at 94, 95 and 96 against the US dollar over the next three, six and 12 months, respectively. On the Union Budget 2027-28,Â  Sengupta said,"the underlying fiscal consolidation or sticking to that path will continue. I think the expenditure allocation towards capex also sort of remains constant as a share of GDP".

Goldman Sachs upgraded India to 'overweight' and set a Nifty target of 28,500 by end-2027, citing expected mid-teen earnings growth, strong domestic demand and relatively low foreign investor positioning.   It said India remains an attractive destination for investors seeking diversification amid global artificial intelligence-related market uncertainties.

Home / Industry / News / India's power demand growth to average 8.5% in FY27, says ICRA report

India's power demand growth to average 8.5% in FY27, says ICRA report Electricity demand rose 11.7 per cent in April-October, while low coal inventories and weather-related uncertainties remain key risks despite robust consumption trends

India's electricity demand rose 11.7 per cent during April-October FY27, while coal stocks at thermal power plants remained below the normative requirement. | Image: Bloomberg

Sudheer Pal Singh New Delhi 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 18 2026 | 5:31 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India's electricity demand growth remained robust at 11.7 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in the first seven months (April-October) of the current financial year, and in line with the trend, it is expected to average 8.5 per cent for FY27, though weather-related uncertainties remain a key risk, ratings agency ICRA said on Wednesday.   Data from Grid Controller of India Limited (GCIL) indicates that the country's electricity demand registered growth of 12.9 per cent during the first 11 days of November 2026, reflecting the continuation of strong demand trends seen during FY27.   This was supported by above-normal temperatures across most parts of the country, which sustained cooling demand despite the onset of the winter season. "Continued festive activity, healthy industrial and commercial consumption, and robust agricultural demand also contributed to higher electricity usage during the period," the agency said.     Coal stocks at thermal power plants stood at around seven days as of November 11, 2026, marginally higher than the levels seen in October 2026, reversing the declining trend observed over the past few months.   However, inventories remained significantly below the normative requirement of around 19-20 days, leaving a relatively thinner buffer against potential demand and fuel supply disruptions. Domestic coal production declined by 1.1 per cent in the first six months of FY27, largely due to lower output from Coal India. However, coal supply to the power sector increased by 5.1 per cent during the period. Also Read

Metal meltdown: SAIL, NALCO, Hindalco drag Nifty Metal 2% lower; here's why

"A further decline in stock levels, particularly if accompanied by weaker coal production or supply constraints, may limit the sector’s ability to meet any sharp surge in peak demand. Sustained recovery in coal production and supply remains important to maintain adequate buffer stock levels," ICRA said.   Spot power tariffs on the Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) averaged ₹4 per unit as of November 10, 2026, declining from ₹6.7 per unit in October 2026, while remaining above ₹3.1 per unit recorded in November 2025.   While tariffs moderated on a sequential basis due to adequate supply availability, particularly during solar hours, they remained higher than the year-ago level, supported by healthy electricity demand. The tariff trend in FY27 will continue to depend on the evolving demand-supply balance and the pace of capacity additions.   More From This Section

item.content:encoded:
Home / Technology / Tech News / Tech outages no coincidence, AI making cyberattacks easier: Nikesh Arora

Tech outages no coincidence, AI making cyberattacks easier: Nikesh Arora US banks, airlines and tech firms face outages, with Apple, Microsoft and Google services hit. Palo Alto CEO Nikesh Arora warns AI is making cyberattacks easier

Nikesh Arora, chairman and chief executive officer (CEO) of Palo Alto Networks | Image: www.paloaltonetworks.in

Vrinda Goel New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 18 2026 | 9:55 AM IST

Listen to This Article

A string of technology outages in the US over the past week has disrupted airlines, banks and major technology services. In the latest incident on Tuesday, Apple and Google users reported problems accessing iCloud, Apple Pay, Gmail and Google Search, among other services.   Against this backdrop, Nikesh Arora, chairman and chief executive officer (CEO) of California-based cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks, has warned that artificial intelligence (AI) is making it easier for hackers to target multiple customers.   Taking to X early Wednesday, Arora said the disruptions were not coincidental and warned enterprises about the growing threat posed by AI-enabled cyberattacks.   "So what the industry tried to warn enterprises about 6 months ago is here. The events of this week so far are not a coincidence. AI is making it easy for hackers to attack multiple customers. All incident responders are busy, unfortunately there is no silver bullet," Arora wrote.

He urged enterprises to run a multi-model testing harness across their infrastructure, patch their code and find virtual patching solutions for open-source software. "When it happens, because it will. Your SOC should be ready to detect and remediate in record time," he said. Also Read

India facing economic disaster, unemployment crisis: Rahul Gandhi in US

Nvidia stops shipping Hopper AI chips to China despite US approval

Delhi air pollution: AQI drops to 214; Grap-III curbs go, schools reopen

Google flags first autonomous AI cyberattack, warns of growing threats

Quad leaders back $85 mn AI push, Mumbai business forum at Manila summit

Arora also called on companies to revamp their security operations centres (SOCs), recommending a real-time data lake with proactive machine learning (ML) detectors across their data and AI-powered correlation. He warned that reactive solutions operating across multiple data lakes were not an adequate plan.   In Tuesday's incident, Downdetector data indicated that iCloud and Apple Pay were among the most affected services, followed by Gmail, Google Search and the App Store. Users reported difficulties with account logins, messaging, emails, digital payments and fund transfers.

Apple said it was working to restore its systems after an internal update caused an outage affecting customer services, including iCloud and Apple Pay. The issue was not caused by a cyberattack, the company said, adding that many of the systems were back up and running, Reuters reported.   ALSO READ: GTA 6: How Latina characters in video game history paved way for Lucía

A week of major technology outages in the US   The Apple outage follows a series of technology disruptions in the US in recent days.   The first outage was reported on November 12, when Microsoft Outlook, Teams and Copilot went down for millions of users globally. The disruption affected organisations, including government departments, businesses and airlines, which were unable to use the services.

On November 13, the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop following a communications outage, with more than 10,000 flights cancelled or delayed. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a newly installed router repeatedly sent large numbers of connection attempts across the FTI network, disrupting aircraft communications and radar feeds at 17 control centres.   On November 16, thousands of customers in the US struggled to access their bank accounts. Many reported problems while trying to make transactions or even use their cards at ATMs. JPMorgan Chase, the largest US bank, later confirmed that a software bug within its systems had caused the outage.

United Airlines also faced technology problems on the same day. The airline was forced to delay flights as it worked to fix the outage. According to a Reuters report, a company-wide web-based outage affected multiple applications used by pilots, including crew communications.   In another incident, a cybersecurity breach involving Optimizely, a platform widely used by websites for services such as A/B testing, was reported. According to media reports, researchers found that a hacker had used the platform to inject malware into websites linked to 178 companies. These included Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce, Ikea and Air France-KLM.
